sections.title: Fats
sections.narration: 11.5 grams of fat. Omega 3 is 1480 milligrams, supporting a more useful fat profile. Cholesterol is 142 milligrams, adding to the cardiovascular tradeoff, and for meats, fat quality is a major tradeoff. For meats, fat quality is the main tradeoff.

sections.title: Proteins
sections.narration: 24.6 grams of protein. Essential amino acids score is 9 out of 9, making the protein useful for repair and maintenance. Collagen is 1.5 grams, not adding much structural protein, so for meats, that collagen side of the protein score stays weak. For meats, protein quality matters a lot.

sections.title: Vitamins
sections.narration: Vitamin B12 is 370% daily value, useful for nerve and blood-cell support. Vitamin D is 24% daily value, not bringing much bone or immune support, so that's a small downside for meats. For meats, vitamin B12 and vitamin D matter most.

sections.title: Minerals
sections.narration: Iron is 16% daily value, useful for oxygen transport. Potassium is 8% daily value, not bringing much fluid-balance support. For meats, iron and zinc can add real value.

sections.title: Pros
sections.narration: The upsides first: small-fish nutrient density is elite. Omega-3s, protein, and micronutrients all come together unusually well here. Easy to centre a meal around. Practical meal value matters. Gives a straightforward protein solution. The category often wins on simplicity and reliability.
